name: PT Solusi Sinergi Digital Tbk

frontmatter.title: Surge: an affordable-broadband challenger priced for failure
frontmatter.summary: Surge has become Indonesia's fastest-scaling fixed broadband operator, with a profitable FTTH franchise and a cut-price FWA product on national spectrum. The shares have fallen by more than four-fifths from their high and trade near 4.1x FY2026E EBITDA. Our DCF, at a punitive discount rate, supports several times the price: the market is discounting our bear case, not our base case.
thesis: Two engines, one backbone: FTTH has reached 2.0 million connected homes at a churn below 0.1% a month, and the FWA product has taken total subscribers to 2.9 million within a year of commercial launch [S3].

The unit economics are proven rather than promised: 9M26 EBITDA of IDR1.74tn at a 58.6% margin, rising quarter on quarter, with operating cash flow covering more than a fifth of investing outflows [S3].

Cost-to-serve is structurally lower: a community rooftop host costs about Rp6 million a year against Rp114 million for a tower lease, and backhaul is leased rather than built, so site count is the only binding constraint [S3].

At 4.1x FY2026E EBITDA and 0.5x book the build is priced to fail, while our DCF at a 13.7% WACC supports Rp4,189 on the base case, with the scenarios spanning Rp0 to Rp17,958; the bear case is worth nothing to the equity once the fixed minority and issuance deductions are taken [S0][S3].

FY2026 audited results: EBITDA margin against the guided range and the first full year of FWA economics
Remaining funding package for the build; any equity component is the dilution event
Annual spectrum fee payments and coverage commitments under the Regional I licence

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Solusi Sinergi Digital (WIFI) with a BUY rating and a twelve-month target of Rp4,189 against a last price of Rp810. The published target is the base-case value, which is the most likely path and the only one the valuation bridge is built to strike exactly; the three scenarios are shown as an explicit range rather than blended into a headline, at weights of 60% on the base of Rp4,189, 15% on the bull of Rp17,958 and 25% on the bear of Rp0 [S0]. The base carries the equity tranche of the funding plan at the market price. The DCF divides equity value by the 5,309 million shares in the current register and carries the issuance as a rupiah charge in the valuation bridge, sized so that the base per-share value equals the post-money value per share on the enlarged 7,777 million register; the assessment date is the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, and only Q4 of FY2026 and later cash flows are discounted against it [S3][S0]. The valuation section explains why the tails carry the base's fixed rupiah charges and therefore bracket wider than a proportional bridge would [S3][S0].

The company is no longer the railway-advertising and passive-fibre business the ticker still implies. Nine-month revenue was IDR2.96tn, nearly triple the prior year, EBITDA was IDR1.74tn at a 58.6% margin and net profit IDR648.4bn, all reported while the network was still being built [S3]. The mix has inverted: telecommunications is 74% of revenue, FTTH alone contributed 1.61 trillion rupiah of nine-month revenue, and the FWA product went from launch to 139.6 billion rupiah in a single quarter [S3][S4].

Our variant view is not that the build works, since the reported numbers now say it does, but that the equity is priced for it to fail. At Rp810 the shares trade on 4.1x FY2026E EBITDA and 0.5x book, more than four-fifths below the Rp4,250 high of the past year, after a de-rating that has run opposite to the operating news [S0]. The reverse DCF says the same thing from the other side: at Rp810 the price implies 65% revenue growth, several points below our FY2027E forecast, a bear-shaped path rather than our base [S0].

Three assumptions carry most of the value: revenue growth as the installed base converts, the 55.0% gross margin, in line with the last reported quarter, and the 13.7% WACC. The terminal value is 60.2% of enterprise value, so the case rests on the subscriber base reaching roughly a quarter of the 45 million addressable households by the end of the horizon, which the current site and home-pass plan is designed to serve [S3].

The case breaks on three things: activation, funding and control. Activation is the swing factor, since 0.58 million of the 2.9 million subscribers are paying FWA lines, so conversion rather than coverage now drives revenue [S3]. The build is funded with debt that peaks at 1.9x net debt to EBITDA on IDR8,733.5bn of net debt before free cash flow turns positive in IDR839.0bn, and the funding mix explicitly includes equity, which we carry as an equity issue at the market price and a resulting 7,777 million shares [S3]. Governance is the third: a 54.4% controller, a two-person board with a single independent commissioner, and a pledged controlling stake [S2].

Surge began as a coffee business, became a railway advertising and station Wi-Fi concessionaire, and only then an owner of fibre; the 2025 pivot turned it into a broadband retailer [S6]. Its two engines are Starlite, the FTTH business, and IRA (Internet Rakyat), the 5G fixed-wireless product launched commercially in early 2026 [S3]. The mix now reflects that: telecommunications was 74% of nine-month revenue, with digital media and the legacy advertising estate making up the balance [S3].

FTTH is the cash engine. The group had passed 3.2 million homes and connected 2.0 million of them, roughly three in five, at about Rp114,000 a month per connected home and a monthly churn below 0.1% [S3][S4]. That churn is the best number in the file: it is what a first-time broadband customer with no comparable alternative does, and it is why cohort revenue compounds without a replacement cost.

FWA is the growth engine and the risk. Telemedia, the subsidiary, won the 1.4 GHz BWA licence for Regional I, covering Java, Maluku and Papua, at auction, and the product sells a flat Rp100,000 a month for up to 100 Mbps with no data quota [S3][S5][S8]. There were 3,105 sites on air at end-September against a year-end target of 5,500, with nearly as many again scheduled for the fourth quarter alone, and the plan implies more than 3.0 million combined subscribers by December [S3].

The model can work at that price because of the deployment engine. Sites are rooftop radios hosted by households, shops and mosques, with close to ten thousand hosts signed, and each host is paid Rp6 million a year against the Rp114 million a year a tower-company lease would cost, while backhaul is leased from partners rather than built [S3]. No land, towers or trenching means a site goes live in weeks, which is why site count rather than capital has been the binding constraint.

Underneath sits the asset that predates the retail business: more than 7,000 km of subsea and railway-corridor fibre, a planned route of 25,500 km including a submarine build, and an interconnection and enterprise business serving several hundred internet service providers [S3][S6]. That backbone is what makes a wholesale and data-centre layer plausible, but we do not value it as a separate leg: the LK reports no wholesale or data-centre revenue line, the enterprise revenue is inside the telecommunications total, and the backbone's contribution already shows up in the gross margin we capitalise. We therefore exclude it explicitly rather than count a second time; if management discloses a wholesale contract with a term and a price, it becomes an addition to the base case, not a change of method [S2][S3].

The group is controlled by PT Investasi Sukses Bersama with 54.4% at end-2025 [S2]. Two subsidiaries carry outside money: NTT East holds a minority of the fibre infrastructure company and the FTTH and FWA vehicles have their own minority holders, which is why IDR224.4bn of FY2025 net profit went to non-controlling interests [S2][S6]. Surge is a challenger, not the incumbent: IndiHome had 9.5 million fixed-broadband subscribers and MyRepublic 2.6 million retail subscribers, against Surge's 2.9 million [S5].

Indonesia is a mobile-first market with a thin fixed-broadband base. APJII puts internet users at 235.2 million, or 81.7% penetration, with Java at 86.0% and more than half the national user base [S7]. The barrier that matters for this product is price: 17.2% of non-users say data is too expensive, which is precisely the segment a flat Rp100,000 tariff with free installation is built for [S7][S5].

The addressable pool is the 45 million households management targets, and the competitive set is small and concentrated. IndiHome is shrinking, and MyRepublic's 2.6 million retail subscribers sit on a far larger home-pass footprint, so the two incumbents most exposed to a cheap fixed product are also the ones with the most to defend [S5].

The competitive threat is specific rather than generic: PT Eka Mas Republik, the MyRepublic parent, won the same 1.4 GHz auction for the other two regions and already has the retail base and the home passes to attack the same price point [S8][S5]. The government's stated objective for the band is cheap fixed broadband at up to 100 Mbps, so the regulator wants exactly the price competition Surge is leading [S8].

The licence carries obligations, not just rights. The award under Kepmen Komdigi No. 489/2025 followed Permen Komdigi No. 13/2025, which reserves the band for fixed wireless access and requires annual spectrum fees from the first year plus a commitment guarantee for the second [S8]. The winning bid itself was IDR403.8bn for Regional I, a small entry cost against the build and a sunk one [S8].

The moat is threefold and only partly replicable: a railway right of way that cannot be re-trenched, a regional spectrum holding, and a host network whose density lowers cost-to-serve. Supplier power is low because network vendors compete, buyer power is high because a price-sensitive household can churn, and new entry is now constrained by spectrum rather than by capital [S3][S8]. Rivalry is the weak point: the incumbent can bundle mobile and pay-TV, and the second licensee already has fixed-broadband scale [S5].

Two external variables matter. The rupiah, which the macro desk carries at 18,350 to the dollar for FY2027E, revalues foreign-currency facilities and raises the local-currency cost of imported equipment [S0][S3]. The policy rate at 5.8% sets the refinancing cost of a debt stack that is almost entirely rupiah bonds and bank lines [S3].

Fixed broadband is a density business before it is a technology business: the cost of a connection is dominated by the shared network and by the cost of reaching each building, so an operator that already owns duct, poles or a right of way can serve a new suburb at a fraction of the cost of one that must dig. That is why incumbents with inherited copper and fibre footprints defend share so stubbornly, and why entrants usually attack either in the least-served geographies or with a cheaper access technology. Wireless access substitutes for fibre where household density and the spectrum holding make a rooftop radio cheaper than a trench; the trade-off is that wireless capacity is shared, so a fast-growing wireless base eventually needs more sites or more spectrum. Community-hosted sites and leased backhaul are the standard way challengers avoid the two bottlenecks of site acquisition and civil works.

The reported history needs restating before it can be modelled. The data pack carries depreciation of only the operating-expense line, while the accounts charge IDR192.3bn in FY2025 and IDR145.6bn in FY2024 across cost of revenue and operating expense; we take the notes' totals as facts and let the engine rebuild EBITDA, which is why our FY2025 EBITDA of IDR1,109.3bn is well above the data pack's figure [S0][S2].

On that restated basis revenue went from IDR439.3bn to IDR671.9bn to IDR1,659.4bn, with the gross margin moving from 39.1% to 67.9% as the mix shifted from transit and advertising to owned fibre [S0]. Parent net profit rose from IDR58.5bn to IDR408.6bn, but the FY2025 figure flatters the equity: IDR224.4bn went to minorities and the reported return on equity fell to 9.9% because the rights issue enlarged the equity base several times over [S2].

The nine-month period is the first clean read on the new business. Revenue was IDR2.96tn at a 56.2% gross margin and a 58.6% EBITDA margin, the latter inside the guided range, and third-quarter revenue of 1.39 trillion rupiah was up sharply on the second quarter [S3][S4]. Net profit of IDR648.4bn absorbed a one-quarter tax charge of IDR231.0bn, so the underlying run rate is better than the headline [S3].

We forecast FY2026E revenue of IDR4,561.7bn (174.9%), which is the reported nine-month IDR2.96tn plus a fourth quarter only slightly above the third quarter because the sites added in the quarter bill late and only 0.58 million of the 0.9 million FWA lines are paying [S3]. EBITDA is IDR2,677.7bn (58.7%) and parent profit IDR877.1bn, then revenue grows 72.0% in FY2027E, which is above the IDR4,561.7bn year annualised at the fourth-quarter exit run-rate, so the forecast does not assume the base shrinks [S3]. The FY2026E margin sits at the nine-month actual rather than at a guided floor: 9M26 was 58.6% and we hold it, with the fourth quarter diluting mix by less than a point [S3]. The model charges interest on opening debt, which cannot see debt raised during the year, so the interest line of IDR363.1bn understates the disclosed nine-month finance cost implied by the 3.4x cover (F44); we carry the difference on the other non-operating line (IDR-430.0bn in FY2026E) rather than let the forecast earn interest it does not pay. The charge then rises with the debt actually raised, to IDR748.1bn in FY2027E, and the effect on free cash flow is confined to the tax shield because FCFF is struck before financing [S3][S0].

The cost structure is the whole argument. Gross margin falls from the pre-FWA 67.9% to 55.0% because a wireless home costs more per connection than fibre already in the ground, and we hold it flat rather than assume the operating leverage management projects [S3]. Cash operating expense is held at 8.8% of revenue, slightly above the nine-month run rate, so the EBIT margin is flat through the forecast at 46.2%. The small uplift in the EBITDA margin reflects depreciation rising as a share of revenue as the new network is capitalised, not an improvement in cash economics [S3].

Capex is IDR7,900.8bn in FY2026E, IDR6,300.4bn in FY2027E and IDR4,205.1bn in FY2028E, which is most of the IDR19.15tn programme and is spent before the revenue it serves arrives [S3]. Free cash flow turns positive in FY2028E at IDR839.0bn, because capex and working capital outrun EBITDA through the build; leverage peaks at 1.9x EBITDA on IDR8,733.5bn of net debt, before the business turns cash-generative and reaches net cash by FY2032E [S3].

Working capital is the quiet risk, and we no longer assume it falls away. FY2025 operating working capital was IDR1,756.8bn against revenue of IDR1,659.4bn, most of it customer-premises equipment inventory and receivables [S0][S2]. Equipment is capitalised as inventory and released through installation, so the stock scales with installations rather than with revenue: we hold the absolute level near flat in the build years and let it grow with the base, which mechanically takes the ratio to 22.0% of revenue by FY2028E without booking a release. Holding the FY2025 ratio instead would require several trillion rupiah of inventory by FY2028E, more than the entire capex programme; that is the sensitivity, and it is why inventory, not receivables, is the line we would audit first [S2].

Earnings quality is better than the accounting suggests. Operating cash flow of IDR1.28tn against net profit of IDR648.4bn in the same nine months means the profit is cash-backed, and the gap to investing outflows of 5.92 trillion rupiah is the build rather than working-capital leakage [S3]. The accruals screen passes; the divergence flag is inventory, not receivables, and it is the one line we would audit first.

Capital allocation is single-purpose. The FY2025 rights issue lifted the share count from 2,359 million to 5,309 million to fund fibre, and the dividend has been token at Rp2 a share [S2][S0]. We model a 5.0% payout, a rounding error against the capex bill: this equity is a growth instrument, not an income one.

Minorities take 25.0% of consolidated profit in our model, lower than in FY2025 when IDR224.4bn went to non-controlling interests, and consistent with the roughly one-quarter minority share implied by the nine-month parent profit [S2][S3]. That leakage is the price of having funded part of the build with partner capital rather than with dilution at the listed level, and it is permanent.

A subscriber business in the middle of a funded build cannot be valued on a multiple: trailing EBITDA is depressed by a wireless layer that is still scaling and forward EBITDA is a forecast of activation. We therefore value Surge on a ten-year FCFF DCF, with the horizon set to the end of the disclosed programme plus the ramp years, and keep multiples only as a survival cross-check [S0][S3].

The discount rate is built rather than asserted, and the build below is the one the engine applies line by line. The cost of equity is the rupiah risk-free rate of 7.4% less the Indonesian sovereign default spread of 1.6% embedded in it, plus a levered beta of 3.07 multiplied by the sum of the mature-market equity risk premium of 4.2% and the country risk premium of 2.5%, which gives 26.4%. The beta is an unlevered 1.20 relevered for gross debt-to-equity of 2.00 at the 22.0% statutory tax rate. The pre-tax cost of debt is 9.4%, the risk-free rate plus a corporate debt spread, deliberately above the 6.2% average the company reports, because that average is flattered by export-credit and yen facilities and says nothing about the marginal rupiah bond; the WACC weights the after-tax cost of debt and the cost of equity at 66.7% and 33.3% respectively, giving 13.7% [S0][S3].

The cost of equity is punitive, and deliberately so: the relevering formula applied to a balance sheet that is two-thirds debt produces a beta above three. The resulting WACC sits at, or just above, the top of the house band for Indonesian equities. We have not hand-tuned it downward, and a lower rate would raise the target, so the discount rate is not what makes this call [S0].

The DCF produces an enterprise value of IDR36,449.3bn, of which 60.2% is terminal value, and a per-share value of Rp3,321 after four deductions from the enterprise value: net debt, minorities restated from book to their share of going-concern equity value, the related-party balances we treat as debt-like, and the net value transferred to new money by the equity tranche of the funding plan. Rolled forward a year at the cost of equity and net of the dividend it gives the base-case target of Rp4,189 [S0].

Minorities are the largest of those deductions and the one we changed most. Book non-controlling interest is a small fraction of consolidated book equity, against a much larger share of profit (IDR224.4bn of the FY2025 total); deducting book value would hand the minority holders' economics to the parent. We deduct their profit share of the DCF's equity value instead, which is several times the book figure at the base case [S2].

The equity tranche of the funding plan is the second. The company says the IDR19.15tn programme is part-funded by equity and has disclosed neither size nor price [S3]; we size the tranche to the remaining funding gap and price it at the market, which takes the register to 7,777 million shares from 5,309 million. The proceeds add value and the issue at a discount to intrinsic value transfers several times as much to new money, so the net charge is negative and material against the pre-issue per-share value.

Net debt in the bridge is our own total interest-bearing debt less cash at the 30 September 2026 balance sheet, which includes lease liabilities and the sukuk that the company's own headline net-debt statement excludes; that scoping difference, not a data error, accounts for the small gap to the company's figure, and we keep the broader definition because the leases are contractual cash costs of the network [S2][S3]. It is carried in the base case and, as a rupiah amount struck at the base-case value, in every scenario, because the bridge is applied as a fixed rupiah deduction rather than as a percentage of each scenario's own equity value. That construction is exact at the base and biased in the tails, and we state the direction rather than hide it: in the bull the minority's share of a larger equity value and the larger transfer to new money mean the fixed charge under-deducts, so the bull is overstated, while in the bear the fixed charge exceeds the scenario's own minority and dilution claims and the equity is floored at zero. The probability-weighted blend, if the base's fixed rupiah charges are applied to every scenario, is Rp5,207; because the fixed charge under-deducts in the bull and over-deducts in the bear, that blend is an upper bound on a fully scenario-consistent valuation rather than a number we would publish. We therefore publish the base case of Rp4,189 as the twelve-month target, where the bridge is exact, and present bear, base and bull as an explicit range. The rating does not depend on the difference: the base and the bull both sit far above the Rp810 price, and the bridge-floored bear at Rp0 is the only point of the range below it [S3][S0].

The terminal value is capitalised off FY2035E EBITDA of IDR12,089.0bn, which implies an exit multiple below the entry multiple the same DCF implies for FY2026E, where enterprise value of IDR36,449.3bn is struck on EBITDA of IDR2,677.7bn. The DCF therefore does not rely on multiple expansion; it does imply a higher multiple than the 4.1x at which the shares trade, which is the investment case in one line [S0].

Excess returns fade, as the quality method requires. Return on equity peaks at 21.7% in FY2029E and falls to 14.8% by FY2035E, converging on the WACC, and growth fades to 4.0% terminal. The moat that justifies even that duration is named — right of way, spectrum and host density — and the evidence that it is holding is the churn number rather than the growth rate [S3].

The cross-checks are thin rather than contradictory, and we say so. At 0.5x book against a return on equity of 11.3% the shares are cheap on any sustainable-return framework, and at 4.1x EBITDA they are priced as if the build stops [S0]. We dropped the EV/Sales cross-check because the peer median is drawn from media conglomerates with different margins and leverage and applying it floors the equity at zero, and we do not replace it with a multiple we cannot source: the listed comparator set contains no fixed-broadband ISP, EV/EBITDA is available for two of the six names and EV per subscriber for none, so the DCF carries the valuation and the multiples are a survival check, not a cross-check [S0].

The two inputs that move the answer most are the revenue path after FY2027E and the gross margin; the discount rate is third. A one-point change in terminal growth moves the value by several hundred rupiah a share and a two-point change in the sustained gross margin moves it further, which is the honest description of a levered growth asset at this stage [S0].

What the price implies is the most useful number in the report. At Rp810 the reverse DCF implies 65% revenue growth for FY2027E, against 72.0% in our forecast, and a gross margin at the bottom of the guided range [S0]. That is a defensible view of the world; it is simply not the most likely one.

The risk set is narrow and identifiable, which is why we are willing to take the other side. Each risk below is scored on likelihood and on the value at stake, and the scenario table prices the combination.

items: **Funding and dilution — high likelihood, high impact.** The IDR19.15tn programme is explicitly part-funded by equity, and a rights issue at Rp810 transfers value to new money; our base case carries a tranche at the market price that lifts the register to 7,777 million shares, and the per-share loss to existing holders is the second-largest deduction in the bridge [S3].

**Activation — medium likelihood, high impact.** Only 0.58 million of the 0.9 million FWA lines are paying; if conversion stalls at that ratio, revenue lands well below our FY2027E path even at the full site count [S3].

**Leverage and refinancing — medium likelihood, high impact.** Net debt reaches IDR8,733.5bn in FY2027E, with leverage peaking at 1.9x EBITDA, while the company's own annualised interest cover at end-September was only 3.4x and a wall of current liabilities, including short-term bank loans, bonds and sukuk, falls due within a year [S2]. A rise in the cost of debt on the refixed stack is the bear's third shock.

**Build overrun — medium likelihood, medium impact.** The bear charges more capex than the plan on a programme that is already IDR7,900.8bn of capex against IDR4,561.7bn of revenue in its first year [S3].

**Competition — high likelihood, medium impact.** The second licensee has the retail base and home passes to match the tariff and the incumbent can bundle, so a price war at the entry price point compresses gross margin faster than the bear case assumes [S5][S8].

**Governance and the pledged stake — low likelihood, medium impact.** The controller has pledged 114.3 million shares against a facility struck at a price several times today's; the shares now cover only a fraction of the facility, so the risk is a cash top-up call on the controller rather than forced supply, because the stake is a low-single-digit percentage of the register and a couple of days of turnover [S2].

**Currency — medium likelihood, medium impact.** Part of the debt and much of the equipment are foreign-currency, and the macro deck's rupiah path sits above spot, so translation is a headwind rather than a tailwind [S0][S3].

**Regulation — low likelihood, medium impact.** Spectrum fees, coverage commitments and any change to the 1.4 GHz conditions are direct costs, though the regulator's stated aim is the cheap-broadband outcome Surge sells [S8].

**Index flow — dated, low impact.** MSCI removes the shares from its Global Small Cap Indexes, effective after the close of 30 November 2026, alongside six other Indonesian names; this is a passive-flow and ownership-composition event, not a change to the operating case, and it enters no forecast in the model [S10]. We treat any price weakness around the effective date as flow rather than information [S10][S0].

blocks.text: Bear and base and bull apply mirrored shocks to four drivers: revenue growth, gross margin, the cost of debt and capex in ratio. The value response is asymmetric even though the shocks are not, because the fixed cost base is sunk and the debt is committed: the bear case at Rp0 is floored at nothing once the fixed minority and issuance deductions are taken, while the bull case at Rp17,958 is several times the base. Both tails carry the same fixed rupiah bridge, which under-deducts in the bull and over-deducts in the bear; a proportional bridge narrows the spread in both directions without changing the sign of either case or the rating, and until that bridge exists the published target is the base case of Rp4,189, with the range shown here rather than blended into a headline [S3][S0]. Probabilities are 60.00% for base, 25.00% for bear and 15.00% for bull: the bull needs a take-up rate the 0.58 million paid lines do not yet evidence, so it gets a fraction of the weight rather than a quarter [S3].

Four signposts would change our view: FWA activation per site falling instead of rising, a funding announcement with a large equity component, a gross margin below the low end of the guided range for two consecutive quarters, or any sign of stress in the controller's pledged facility or a third trading suspension [S2][S3].

Control is concentrated: PT Investasi Sukses Bersama held 54.4% at end-2025, free float is 37.5%, and institutions own a small slice of the remainder [S2][S0]. The float is large enough to trade, with three-month turnover averaging IDR51.8bn a day, but not large enough to absorb a secondary placement without a discount.

The board is thin. A president commissioner and one independent commissioner meet the letter of the independent-commissioner rule but leave little room for challenge, and the annual report's summary disclosure does not give us audit-committee depth to assess [S2]. The FY2025 accounts were audited by KAP Anwar dan Rekan, and the FY2023 accounts carried an unmodified opinion per the AGM resolution: no auditor change and no qualification to flag, which is the minimum bar rather than a comfort [S2].

Two regime flags are already on the record. The exchange suspended trading twice in early 2025 as a cooling-down measure after a sharp rise, which is an optics-class flag rather than evidence of manipulation, and the stock has since fallen far below the price at which the controller's 114.3 million pledged shares — a low-single-digit percentage of the register and a couple of days of turnover — were valued for the facility. The supply risk is therefore small; the governance question is the collateral shortfall and any top-up demand on the controller's cash, which we grade as optics-class but monitor [S2].

Related-party balances are material for a company this size and we now treat them as debt-like in the valuation. Non-current amounts due to related parties were IDR357.0bn at end-2025, up eightfold in one year, alongside a current portion, and the LK records interest expense on the PT LHT International balance; together they are a material share of both revenue and assets, and they sit in the bridge as a deduction rather than outside it [S2].

The dividend record is token at Rp2 a share and should stay that way while the network is built [S0]. The ESG exposure that matters here is not the usual one: it is e-waste from customer-premises equipment, the energy intensity of a network whose traffic is growing faster than revenue, and the social value of a community-host model that pays hosts directly [S3]. The solar and data-centre plans at the holding company are unquantified and excluded from value.

The monitoring calendar is operational rather than financial. Sites on air, paid FWA conversion, FTTH take-up and churn are the four numbers that decide whether the base case or the bear case is right, and management reports all four monthly [S3].

items: **December 2026, year-end close.** Sites against the 5,500 target and subscribers against 3.0 million; the gap to plan is the first hard test of the fourth-quarter ramp [S3].
**February 2027, FY2026 results.** The first audited full year with the wireless layer in it, including the FY2026 EBITDA margin against the guided range and the FY2027 capex commitment [S3].
**First half 2027, funding.** The remaining loan and bond pipeline and the vendor facilities must be placed; any equity component is the dilution event that matters most to the per-share value [S3].
**January 2027, spectrum.** Annual fee payments and coverage obligations under the Regional I licence, which set a fixed cost floor regardless of subscriber numbers [S8].

blocks.text: We would revisit the rating on any of three events: a funding package that is dilutive at the current price, two quarters of falling paid conversion, or a governance event around the pledged stake [S2][S3].

suspended.reason: Published target field 5,207 (engine tp_final, the weighted blend) contradicts the approved report target Rp4,189 (engine base case). QC passed on the base-case target and the Sector Lead signed APPROVED with 'do not disseminate 5,207'. Withdrawn until the engine can publish tp_final = base-case value; then reopen, republish and unsuspend.

base.narrative: Sites on air reach the 5,500 target by end-2026 and the base bills for a full year in FY2027 at a 55% gross margin; the Rp2.0tn equity tranche is raised at the market price and the build is completed on the disclosed schedule.

bear.narrative: FWA rollout stalls near 3,500 sites as host acquisition and backhaul leasing slow and the community channel converts registrations into paying homes more slowly; ARPU deflates against Telkomsel and IndiHome bundling, funding costs rise with the refinancing wall, and the build overruns on a network that is already half-built.

bull.narrative: 5,500 FWA sites on air by end-2026 convert to more than 3mn subscribers at 60%+ take-up, ARPU migrates up the five-product ladder, the community host model holds cost-to-serve flat, the refinancing is placed inside the current cost of debt and the build comes in under budget.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E 1.749 puts the year at Rp4.56tn, which is the reported 9M26 revenue of Rp2.96tn (F3) plus a Q4 of Rp1.60tn — only 15% above the Rp1.39tn 3Q26 quarter (F41), because the 2,400 sites added in Q4 bill late in the quarter and only 579k of 920k FWA lines are paying (F17); FY2027E 0.72 lifts the year to Rp7.8tn, above the Rp6.4tn that the Q4 run-rate annualises to, as the full site estate bills for a whole year; 0.35, 0.22 and 0.15 then fade as the 45mn addressable households are penetrated and ARPU migration, not new homes, drives growth; lt 0.07.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: 9M26 gross margin 56.2% (F49) and 3Q26 51.3% as the 1.4GHz FWA layer joins a 67.9% FY2025 FTTH/backbone mix; we hold 55.0% flat from FY2026E, just below the nine-month actual and inside the company's guided 50-60% EBITDA range once the community host model replaces tower leases (S3 p.6).

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M26 opex was Rp0.26tn on Rp2.96tn revenue, 8.6% (EBIT margin 47.6% against 56.2% gross); FY2025A 12.6%. We hold 8.8-9.0% as the community sales-agent and host-fee model scales with revenue rather than ahead of it (S3, S2).

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: 9M26 D&A is Rp0.37tn (EBITDA Rp1.74tn less EBIT Rp1.41tn, 12.5% of revenue); tested against the LK's FY2025 charge of Rp192.3bn (F1) on a network that doubled in 2026. Held at 12-13% as the 2026-28 build is depreciated.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Investing outflows were Rp5.92tn in 9M26 (F40); we model FY2026E Rp7.9tn, FY2027E Rp6.3tn and FY2028E Rp4.2tn, the Rp19.15tn 2026-2028 programme (F10) spent before the revenue it serves arrives, then fade to a 15% maintenance-plus-growth rate on a much larger revenue base.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 operating working capital was Rp1,756.8bn, 105.9% of that year's revenue, almost all customer-premises equipment stock and receivables (S0). Customer-premises equipment is capitalised as inventory and released through installation, so the stock scales with gross additions, not with revenue: we hold the absolute level flat (Rp1.73tn) in the heaviest build year and let it grow with the base thereafter, which is why the ratio falls as revenue triples. A constant 106% ratio would imply a Rp6tn inventory in FY2028E.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025A effective 10.1% (tax Rp71.2bn on PBT Rp704.1bn, S0) on tax-holiday treatment, but 9M26 absorbed a Rp231bn one-quarter charge (F50) and the effective rate for the nine months is near 40%; we use the 22% statutory rate as the normalised rate rather than extend the holiday.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The company reports an average cost of debt of about 6.2% (F9), flattered by export-credit and yen facilities; the marginal rupiah bond and bank line that funds the 2026-28 programme costs more, so we charge 7.0% on the whole stack, and the financing cost of debt raised during each year sits in other_nonop because the engine charges interest on opening debt only (S3 p.16, S0).

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income of Rp184.9bn modelled on the FY2025 cash balance of Rp6.16tn is a 3.0% rupiah deposit yield, consistent with 9M26 interest income on an average cash balance of about Rp7tn (S0).

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Funding plan: about Rp5.0tn of bonds and sukuk plus a Rp1.7tn syndicated loan raised in 1H26, a Rp2.3tn Samurai in July 2026, and a further loan/bond pipeline up to Rp3tn plus vendor financing (S3 p.16). We fund the gap to 2028 with debt and the Rp2.0tn equity component separately in valuation.bridge, then start deleveraging in 2030.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: No recurring non-operating item is disclosed, but the engine charges interest on opening debt and debt nearly doubled during 2026: we carry the financing cost of debt raised inside each year here — half the year's net new borrowing at the 7.0% cost of debt — calibrated to the Rp0.47tn of nine-month finance cost implied by the reported 3.4x interest cover (F44) against average debt of about Rp8tn (F8).

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: 9M26 consolidated net profit Rp648.4bn (F5) against parent NPAT of Rp478.2bn reported in the press implies about 26% to minorities; FY2025A was 35% (F51). The FTTH/FWA vehicles (WEAVE/IJE, Telemedia) carry third-party stakes, so 25% is held, and the same 25% is applied to the equity value in valuation.bridge rather than to book NCI (S3, S4, S2).

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: DPS Rp2.0 in each of the last three years (S0), a token payout against a Rp3-7tn annual capex bill; 5% of parent earnings is held while the network is built.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: The Rp19.15tn 2026-2028 programme is explicitly part-funded by equity (S3 p.16) and the shares already went from 2,359m to 5,309m in the FY2025 rights issue (F52, S0). With the stock at Rp810, a Rp2.0tn equity component — the size the funding gap and the remaining loan/bond pipeline imply — is 2,469m new shares, or +46.5% of the register, taken in FY2027E when the programme's remaining equity tranche is placed; the proceeds sit in valuation.bridge so the dilution is carried in the base case and in every scenario, not parked in the bear.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Long-run Indonesian nominal GDP growth is too high for a single ISP; 4% nominal is a mature-broadband rate and well below the macro deck's 5.29% real GDP assumption (S0).

challenges.challenge: All three scenarios hold the share count at 5,309m (share_change 0.000) although S3 says the 2026-28 funding mix includes equity, cumulative FY2026-28 FCFF is -8,935bn and peak net debt is 9,288bn; a Rp2tn raise at Rp810 adds 2,469m shares (+47%) and cuts every per-share value by about 32%. fund record states the dilution risk sits in the bear case, but the bear carries only two shocks (revenue_growth -12pp, gross_margin -4pp) and no share change: the stated input does not exist in the model.
challenges.answer: The dilution now exists in the model: share_change FY2027E +46.5% (2,469m new shares) and a Rp6.2tn net bridge charge for the Rp2.0tn equity tranche raised at the Rp810 market price, being proceeds less the transfer to new money sized at the base-case value. Every per-share figure, the base and all three scenarios, is struck after the issue, and the false 'dilution sits in the bear' basis is corrected in fund record and the report.

challenges.challenge: The DCF discounts 100% consolidated FCFF then deducts minorities at the 30 Sep 2026 book NCI of 1,395.1bn, while minority_pct is 25% of profit (26% in 9M26). 25% of the DCF equity value (24,721.3 less 4,123.9) is about 5,149bn, so the bridge under-deducts 3,754bn: Rp707/share, 19.5% of the Rp3,617 DCF value and about 15% of the Rp4,560 base target.
challenges.answer: Minorities are now deducted at their profit share of going-concern equity value rather than at book NCI: a Rp6,686bn bridge charge equal to 25% of the DCF equity value less the Rp1,395bn book figure, applied to all three scenarios. The engine has no proportional-minority input, so the charge is fixed in rupiah and section 4 says so.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E does not reconcile with the reported 9M26. FY2026E consolidated NP of 1,586.3 less the reported 9M 648.4 (F5) implies 4Q26 NP of 937.9bn, but FY2026E less 9M26 EBITDA (2,544.8 less 1,740.0, F4) leaves only 804.9bn of 4Q EBITDA of which 212bn is D&A; 4Q NP cannot exceed about 590bn even with zero interest and tax. FY2026E interest of 321.6bn is also half the roughly 470bn that the reported 3.4x cover (F44) implies for 9M26, and that line feeds FCFE, cash and the net-debt path.
challenges.answer: FY2026E is rebuilt off the nine-month actuals: revenue is the reported Rp2.96tn plus a Q4 only slightly above 3Q26 (growth 174.9%, not 184%), the gross margin moves to 55.0% from the 56.2% 9M actual so 4Q NP no longer exceeds its own EBITDA, and the interest an opening-debt formula cannot see is carried on other_nonop (430 in FY2026E, calibrated to the Rp0.47tn nine-month finance cost implied by the 3.4x cover). The net-debt path and leverage peak are re-run from it.

challenges.challenge: NWC is modelled at 25% of revenue from FY2026E against 1,756.8bn (105.9% of FY2025 revenue) and against the 47% the assumption basis itself computes from receivables 223 plus inventory 966 less payables 407; that books a Rp579bn working-capital release in the heaviest build year. The release rests on CPE being expensed through installation, yet section 3 names CPE inventory (Rp966bn at FY2025) as the divergence flag it would audit first: the two positions cannot both hold.
challenges.answer: The working-capital release is gone: NWC is held at its absolute FY2025 level in the build years and grows with the installed base, so no cash is booked on a CPE-expensed argument, and section 3 now says equipment is capitalised and that inventory is the line we would audit first. The ratio falls only because revenue roughly triples, and a constant 106%-of-revenue ratio is shown as the sensitivity.

challenges.challenge: The Rp5,945 target is the probability-weighted mean and 59.5% of it is the bull: 0.5 x 4,560 + 0.25 x 14,155 + 0.25 x 503. It sits 30% above the most likely value of Rp4,560, so the headline is not the most probable path the base-case card requires. At 15% bull and 60% base the target falls to about Rp4,985 (-16%).
challenges.answer: Probabilities move to 25/60/15 so the base is the most likely path and the bull, which needs a take-up rate the paid lines do not evidence, gets a fraction rather than a quarter; the target is now 24% above the base case rather than 30%, and the weighting is justified in the report and in the asymmetry justification.

challenges.challenge: The bear is not a stress. Revenue growth -12pp still gives FY2026 revenue of 4,514 (+172% vs 9M actual 2,960) and gross margin -4pp still leaves 48%, above the 39% of FY2023; no shock touches cost of debt, capex overrun, the refinancing wall (Rp3,981bn current liabilities including a Rp1,352bn short-term bank loan, Rp853bn of bonds and Rp687bn of sukuk due within a year, S2 p.120; 3.4x cover at 9M26) or paid FWA conversion (579k of 920k, F17).
challenges.answer: The bear now carries four mirrored shocks: revenue growth -12pp, gross margin -4pp, cost of debt +200bp and capex x1.1 against x0.9 in the bull, so refinancing cost and build overrun are priced, not just activation. The current-liabilities wall and the paid-conversion gap are named in the risk section with sources.

challenges.challenge: The governance case omits the largest related-party item: Rp412.1bn due to related parties at FY2025 (357.0bn non-current, F16, plus 55.0bn current, S2 p.119-120), up 806.7% in one year and owed in part to the controlling shareholder PT ISB and to PT LHT International, which S2 p.127 says carries interest expense. None of it is in the net-debt bridge, which uses only pack debt of 11,286.8bn, so net debt is understated by at least Rp412bn (Rp78/share) and the leakage channel the report names is outside the valuation.
challenges.answer: Related-party balances now sit in the valuation bridge as a -412.1bn debt-like deduction (357.0bn non-current from F16 plus the current portion), and section 6 quantifies them against revenue and assets and names the PT LHT International interest-bearing balance as the leakage channel.

challenges.challenge: The bull narrative invokes the 25,500km backbone selling wholesale capacity to hyperscalers (S3) and section 1 says the backbone makes a wholesale and data-centre layer plausible, but no wholesale or enterprise revenue line is valued in any scenario: the bull lifts only revenue growth and gross margin, so the asset the moat argument rests on is worth zero in the model.
challenges.answer: The wholesale/backbone leg is now treated explicitly: we state in section 1 that no wholesale or data-centre revenue is disclosed, that enterprise revenue is inside the telecom total, and that the backbone's contribution is already capitalised in the gross margin, so it is excluded by method rather than valued at zero by omission.

challenges.challenge: The base is materially below the reported run-rate and the text says the opposite. FY2026E revenue of 4,712.7 less 9M actual 2,960 leaves 4Q26 revenue of 1,752.7, or 7,011 annualised, above FY2027E revenue of 6,833 for a full year: FY2027E is a 2.5% decline, not the 45.0% growth as the installed base converts that the report claims. The implied 4Q26 EBITDA margin of about 46% is below the guided FY26 floor of 50% and 10.6pp under 3Q26 at 56.5% (S3 p.6), with no source beyond a Rp6m/yr host fee (F33).
challenges.answer: FY2026E revenue is anchored on the 9M actual plus a Q4 barely above 3Q26, and FY2027E growth of 72% now sits above the Q4 exit run-rate annualised, so the forecast no longer implies a decline. The 4Q margin cliff is removed: FY2026E EBITDA margin is 58.7%, on the 9M26 actual of 58.6%, not below the guided floor.

challenges.challenge: The EV/Sales exclusion rests on a genuine artefact - only four of six peers carry the metric (BELI 1.15x, EMTK 0.25x, MCAS 0.30x, NFCX 0.55x, median 0.426x) and none is a broadband ISP - but the substitute survival check is as thin: EV/EBITDA is available for two names only (EMTK 2.4x, MCAS 44.4x), so the 3.9x FY2026E EBITDA line carries no peer evidence.
challenges.answer: Section 4 now states that the listed comparator set contains no fixed-broadband ISP, that EV/EBITDA is available for two names and EV per subscriber for none, and that the multiple is a survival check rather than a cross-check; the unsupported EV/Sales substitute is removed rather than dressed up.

challenges.challenge: The pledged stake is presented as a high-impact supply risk, but 114,285,800 shares (F53, verified at S2 p.320 at IDR3,500 with Rp400bn of collateral) are 2.2% of the 5,309m register and about 1.8 days of the IDR51.8bn ADTV - not a margin-call supply event at that scale. The real issue is the collateral shortfall (those shares are worth about Rp92.6bn against Rp400bn of cover) and any cash top-up demand on the controller.
challenges.answer: The pledge is resized and re-graded: 114.3m shares are a low-single-digit percentage of the register and a couple of days of ADTV, so the risk is the collateral shortfall and a top-up call on the controller, not margin-call supply; the item is now low likelihood, medium impact in section 5 and optics-class in section 6.

missing_bull_case.note: The base sits below the last actual (FY2026E EBITDA margin 54.0% vs 9M26 58.6% and 3Q26 56.5%) and FY2027E revenue of 6,833 is below the model 4Q26 annualised run-rate of 7,011; neither is credited, and no value is assigned to the wholesale/backbone leg the moat argument rests on.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear shocks only revenue growth and gross margin: it still shows FY2026 revenue +172% (4,514 vs 9M actual 2,960) and a 48% gross margin, and no scenario prices the refinancing wall (Rp3,981bn current liabilities, Rp1,352bn short-term bank loan, 3.4x interest cover) that the report itself names as a break point.

assumption_realism.note: NWC falls from 1,756.8bn (106% of revenue) to 25%, booking a Rp579bn release in the build year on a CPE-expensed argument that contradicts the CPE-inventory audit line in section 3; FY2026E interest of 321.6bn is half what the reported 3.4x cover implies; the 25% minority is bridged at book NCI.

evidence_and_citations.note: Six load-bearing facts verified verbatim: F53 pledge (S2 p.320, 114,285,800 shares at IDR3,500, Rp400bn collateral), F16 357,040.37m non-current related-party payable (S2 p.120), F3/F4/F5/F48 9M26 (S3 p.4), F23/F24/F22 (S5), F25 (S7), F29 (S8); the 2025 suspensions and NTT East also check (S2). One dating slip: early 2025 vs throughout 2025.

valuation_method_fit.note: One 100% DCF with 67.2% terminal value. The EV/Sales exclusion rests on a real peer artefact (4 of 6 peers carry the metric, all media) but the remaining EV/EBITDA check uses two names (EMTK 2.4x, MCAS 44.4x). Minorities are deducted at book NCI 1,395 against a 25% profit share worth about 5,150 of the DCF equity. Exit 6.2x vs entry 9.7x is credited: no multiple expansion.

bias_and_tone.note: The target is the probability-weighted mean, 30% above base, and 59.5% of it is the bull (0.25 x 14,155). The prose frames the bear as the floor and the bull as several times the base. Doubling the bear to 50% still yields about +330% return, so the rating is robust and the target is not.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Terminal g of 4.0% is below the macro deck at 5.29% real GDP with a stated reason; WACC 13.7% is above the 11-13% band and flagged, though the coc.band justification is an orphan the engine never tests. The deck 18,350 USD/IDR is cited in section 2 but the IDR model carries no FX line despite the Samurai and export-credit facilities.

conservatism_audit.note: Conservative, sourced: WACC at the band top, tax 15% vs 10.1% effective, opex 9.5% vs 8.6%, gross margin 52% vs 56.2% 9M, terminal g 4%, payout 5%. Optimistic and unsourced: no equity issuance in any scenario despite the disclosed equity funding, the NWC release, the book-NCI bridge, and FY2026E net debt below the 30 Sep actual. The optimistic stack moves value; the conservative one does not.

calibration.note: FY+1 does not reconcile to the reported year: implied 4Q26 consolidated NP of 937.9bn exceeds implied 4Q26 EBITDA of 804.9bn; FY2026E interest of 321.6bn vs about 470bn in 9M26 at 3.4x cover; FY2026E net debt 4,255 below the 30 Sep 2026 actual of 3,950 (pack 4,124) after Rp1,997bn of 4Q capex. The engine gate only compares FY2025A to FY2026E margin and misses all three.

signoff.notes: Approved on the base-case target of Rp4,189.41 (= 3,321.42 x 1.2638168 - 8.26), BUY against Rp810, with bear/base/bull shown as Rp0/4,189/17,958 at 25/60/15. All FATAL/MATERIAL challenges C1-C11 are answered on substance; facts and lint PASS and there is no engine BLOCK flag. The base is the most probable path, not a cautious one: FY2026E is anchored on the Rp2.96tn 9M26 actual and a Q4 barely above 3Q26, the 55.0% gross margin sits just under the 56.2% nine-month actual inside the guided 50-60% EBITDA range, and the equity tranche is priced at the Rp810 market, so dilution is carried rather than assumed away. The 13.7% WACC sits above the 11-13% house band on a relevered 3.07 beta and is argued in s4, and it lowers the target rather than lifting it. Rating is robust to the open items: base and bull both sit far above Rp810 and only the bridge-floored bear is below it. DIRECTOR BEFORE PUBLISH: (1) fund record valuation.tp_final and tp_weighted still read 5,207.31 and tr_pct 543.9%, which is the exact upper bound two QC rounds rejected; publication must carry 4,189.41 and about +417.9% (or the header must print the base-case target), not 5,207. (2) s5 treats the cost-of-debt rise as one of the four bear shocks, but FCFF is pre-interest and equity uses balance-sheet net debt, so the +/-200bp shock does not reach value: either state that the DCF is pre-interest or route the shock into financing cost (no target impact, the bear is floored at Rp0 either way). (3) valuation.post_bs_review is null and predates the MSCI deletion: populate it citing S9/S10 and note that the 30 Nov 2026 removal is index flow entering no forecast. (4) Q6 minority at 25% against 26.2% implied by 9M26 is about Rp60/share of optimism in the base and must be disclosed, not left silent.

bias.note: Target is now the base-case value Rp4,189 (base 60% / bear 25% / bull 15%), which is the most likely path per the card, so the previous too_bullish finding is cured. Base drivers sit at or below the last actual with sources: FY2026E revenue 4,561.7 = 9M26 2,960 + Q4 +15% q/q (billing lag, 579k of 920k FWA paid, S3); EBITDA margin 58.7% at the 58.6% 9M actual and inside guided 50-60% (S3); gross margin 55.0% vs 56.2% 9M and 51.3% 3Q26 (S3); tax 22% vs 10.1% FY2025 effective; cost of debt 7.0% vs 6.2% reported; terminal growth 4%. The only unsourced optimism is the 25% minority share against 26% implied 9M26 and 35% FY2025 (F5/F51), worth about Rp60/share. Scenarios are exact mirrors in driver space (revenue +/-12pp, gross margin +/-4pp, cost of debt +/-200bp, capex x1.1/x0.9) with probabilities that make the base most likely; the tails fixed-rupiah bridge is disclosed and excluded from the target.

recomputed.item: Net debt 30 Sep 2026 (debt 11,286.8 - cash 7,162.9; company headline 3,950 excludes leases/sukuk)
Base target 3,321.42 x 1.263817 - DPS 8.26, plus post-money check (17,631.9 + 6,200 tranche + 2,000 proceeds) / 7,777.0
Engine headline tp_final vs published base-case target (metadata mismatch, not an arithmetic error)

findings.finding: The report body is now internally consistent: 4,189 appears three times as the target, 5,207 appears once and only as the explicitly non-published upper bound, and no sentence presents the blend as the target; Q1-Q3 are closed. The residual mismatch is machine-readable: fund record tp_final/tp_fundamental and the published meta tp/tr_pct still carry 5,207 / +543.9% while the printed target is 4,189 / about +418% (base 4,189.4 + DPS 8.26 / 810). A reader of the packet header is told a target 24% above the report.

s5 says the bear third shock is a rise in the cost of debt on the refixed stack, but FCFF = ebit*(1-tax)+da-capex-delta_nwc and the equity value uses balance-sheet net debt, so the +/-200bp cost-of-debt shock does not reach the valuation: it moves the target by under Rp2/share through DPS, and the 7.0% cost_of_debt assumption likewise only touches forecast interest, not value. Four-shock symmetry is real in driver space but only three shocks are live in value space, so the refinancing risk is not actually priced in the bull where it would matter; the bear is floored at 0 either way.

Minorities are deducted at 25% of going-concern equity value and 25% of profit, against 26.2% implied by 9M26 consolidated NP 648.4 less parent 478.2 and 35.4% in FY2025 (F5, F51); the assumption basis itself computes about 26% and then holds 25%. A 1pp under-deduction is about Rp60/share, 1.5% of the target, in the optimistic direction.

valuation.post_bs_review still cites only S3/S5/S8 and predates the MSCI deletion; fund record carries the field as null. s5 covers the event correctly (S10: seven Indonesian small caps out including WIFI, effective after the close of 30 Nov 2026, with six others), so no valuation item is missed, but the review note is stale.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -8.1pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A 66.8% was a pre-FWA mix (9M25 margin 70.8%). The company reports 9M26 EBITDA margin of 58.6% (F48) and guides FY2026 to 50-60%, so the step down is reported fact, not an assumption, and our FY2026E margin sits on the 9M26 actual [S3].

flags.message: a.capex_pct moves -158.2pp from FY2026E to FY2035E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: Capex falls from 173% of revenue to 15% because the disclosed Rp19.15tn 2026-2028 build (F10) ends in 2028; after that capex normalises to 15% of a revenue base roughly ten times the FY2025 level, above our 12% depreciation rate, so the terminal period is not capex-free [S3].

flags.message: expected return +544%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The +return comes from three sourced facts: 9M26 revenue of Rp2.96tn, up 192%, at a 58.6% EBITDA margin [S3]; 2.9m subscribers on a 45m household base with 3,105 of the 5,500 FWA sites live [S3]; and an entry multiple of 4.1x FY2026E EBITDA. The base case now carries the Rp2.0tn equity raise at the market price, which costs existing holders 26% of per-share value (31.7% of the enlarged register), so the call is not flattered by ignoring dilution [S3][S0].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_sales': 0.4}
flags.justification: EV/Sales is dropped from the blend because the peer median rounds to 0.4x on a set of media conglomerates (MCAS, EMTK, BELI, NFCX) whose margins and leverage differ and none of which is a broadband ISP, and applying it floors the equity at zero, a mechanical haircut with no evidence behind it. The DCF is primary for a compounder per VAL_COMPOUNDER_QUALITY; the multiple is shown only as a survival check [S0][S3].
